chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When it is the first night of the month of Ramadan, then say:

O Allah, Lord of the month of Ramadan and Revealer of the Quran! This is the month of Ramadan in which You revealed the Quran, and in which You sent down clear signs from guidance and the Criterion. O Allah, grant us its fasting and help us in its night prayer.

O Allah, preserve it for us, keep us safe therein, and receive it back from us in ease from You and forgiveness. And place in what You decree and ordain from the inevitable matter, in what is distinguished from the Wise command during the Night of Power, from the decree that cannot be returned or changed — that You write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House whose hajj is accepted, whose sa'i is appreciated, whose sins are forgiven, and from whom evil deeds are expiated.
And place in what You decree and ordain that You extend my life-span for me and expand for me from the permissible provision.

key_terms.الرِّزْقُ الْحَلَالُ: Permissible (halal) provision — sustenance acquired through religiously lawful means
key_terms.الْحَجُّ الْمَبْرُورُ: Accepted/righteous hajj — a pilgrimage performed with complete sincerity and fulfillment of its conditions
key_terms.الْفُرْقَانُ: The Criterion (al-Furqan) — one of the names of the Quran, meaning that which distinguishes truth from falsehood
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ الْمَحْتُومُ: The inevitable decree — divine decisions that are absolute and cannot be changed
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Decree — the most sacred night in Ramadan (27th of Ramadan according to most traditions) when angels descend and divine decrees are finalized

ai.seo_question: What supplication (du'a) did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq teach to recite on the first night of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a specific supplication to be recited on the first night of Ramadan, connecting the act of du'a to the cosmic significance of Laylat al-Qadr. The supplication covers all key domains of well-being: spiritual (fasting, night prayer), physical safety, divine forgiveness, acceptance of hajj, and extension of life with halal provision. Early Shia Muslims would have understood this as a way to align oneself with the divine decrees made on Laylat al-Qadr — invoking all blessings simultaneously at the most auspicious moment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa Al Sabaty who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whenever it is the first night a Month of Ramazan, so say,

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Month of Ramazan, and the Revealer of the Quran! This is the Month of Ramazan in which the Quran was Revealed, and there descended in it clear Verses of the Guidance and the Criterion. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace us its Fasts and Aid us upon its establishing. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Give it as a safety for us, Keep us safe therein and Receive it back in safety from us in Ease from You<sup>azwj</sup>, and Forgiveness, and Cause it what You<sup>azwj</sup> have Judged and Ordained from the inevitable Commands, in what the Wise Commands are Made distinct during the Night of Pre-determination, from the Judgement which can neither be returned nor changed, if You<sup>azwj</sup> could Write for me to be from the pilgrims of your<sup>azwj</sup> Sacred House (Kabah), the ones whose Hajj is Accepted, whose Sa’ee (a ritual of Hajj) is Appreciated, ones whose sins are Forgiven, the ones who sins are Remedied,
and Make to be in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Judgement and Ordainment that You<sup>azwj</sup> would Lengthen my life-span for me, and would Expand for me from the Permissible sustenance’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabatiy who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘In the first night of the month of Ramadan say the following:

“O Lord of the month of Ramadan and the One who has revealed the Holy Quran! This is the month of Ramadan when You have revealed the Holy Quran. You have revealed in it clear signs for guidance and discernment. O Lord, grant us the opportunity to fast in this month and assist us to perform salat (prayer).

O Lord, keep it safe for us, keep us safe therein, and take it back from us with ease and forgiveness. O Lord, in Your determination and measures of the inevitable matters and Your discernment of the matters of wisdom, during the night of al-Qadr (destiny), the determinations that will not be changed or altered, please write my name with those who perform Hajj around Your respected House. Please write my name with the names of those whose efforts are appreciated, whose sins are forgiven and bad deeds remedied.
In Your measures and determination, please grant me long life and abundantly lawful sustenance.’””
